key_insight: A GPT2 table-to-text approach can turn small, imbalanced clinical datasets into stronger disease prediction models by leveraging contextual clinical language rather than relying only on traditional statistical learning.
clinical_relevance: This could help surface clinically meaningful patterns in low-volume records and improve prediction performance for conditions with scarce positive cases, while still supporting interpretability.
method: Converted structured patient records into physician-style text.
Used GPT4-generated paraphrasing to augment minority-class examples.
Fine-tuned GPT2 on four public healthcare datasets and applied gradient-based explainability.
evidence_signal: Across heart disease, heart failure, chronic kidney disease, and thyroid cancer recurrence datasets, the model reported average precision, specificity, sensitivity, and F1-score of 0.96, 0.97, 0.96, and 0.96.
watch_item: Results come from public benchmark datasets, so real-world performance and robustness on local clinical data, shifting documentation styles, or rare edge cases may need further validation.
paper_title: Can GPT Be Used as an Alternative Prediction Model to Traditional Machine Learning and Neural Networks on Low-Volume Clinical Data?
